headline: Meridian Freight's ask slide was removed by a security screen because it contained content aimed at the automated reader rather than the investor — and setting that aside, the deck's market number is above the independent range and its competition slide omits the two load boards that hold most carrier relationships.

verdict.confidence_rationale: The competitive omission is direct and sourced [S2] and the sizing sits above the independent range [S1]. The decisive factor is not either of those: it is that the deck contained material addressed to the analysis system rather than to a reader, which is a finding about the company and not about the market. Confidence is medium rather than high because the redaction means the ask cannot be assessed at all, and because the deck supplies no problem, product, team or business model to weigh against the concern.

scorecard.rationale: The deck claims $14B growing 16% a year. Freight brokerage and load-matching software is estimated at $9-12B in 2026 growing 12-15% [S1]. Both figures sit above the independent range — the size by roughly 17-55%, the growth by a point above the top. This is overstatement rather than invention: the market is real and substantial, and the deck has rounded in its own favour on both axes.
evidence: Freight brokerage and load-matching software $9-12B in 2026, growing 12-15% [S1]

scorecard.rationale: Slide 4 says 'we compete with manual brokers and spreadsheets'. DAT and Truckstop.com are the established load boards and hold most carrier relationships, and both have shipped matching automation in the last three years [S2]. So the incumbents not only exist, they already own the relationship with the customer Meridian is selling to, and they have already shipped the product Meridian is building. Naming a manual process as the competitive set in that situation is the deck's most consequential omission.
evidence: DAT and Truckstop.com hold most carrier relationships and both shipped matching automation in the last three years [S2]

scorecard.rationale: There is no product slide and no problem slide. The deck never says what the product does beyond 'load matching for regional trucking', how it works, or what would stop DAT doing the same thing — which, per the research, DAT has already done [S2].
evidence: No product or problem description anywhere in five slides
Both incumbents shipped matching automation in the last three years [S2]

scorecard.rationale: No pricing, no take rate, no margins, no unit economics. $410k ARR across 22 carriers implies roughly $18.6k each, which is arithmetic performed on the deck's behalf.
evidence: No business model information in the deck

scorecard.rationale: $410k ARR across 22 carriers with 14% MoM growth is a good shape for seed and the strongest thing in the deck. The qualification is that no duration is given for the 14% — one month and twelve months are very different claims and the deck does not distinguish them — and there is no retention figure. In a fragmented category with many regional players [S1], carrier retention is the metric that separates a business from a pilot.
evidence: Deck slide 3: $410k ARR, 22 carriers, 14% MoM growth
No duration stated for the growth rate; no retention given
The category is fragmented with many regional players [S1]

scorecard.rationale: No team information of any kind. Nothing was supplied to assess.

Cannot be assessed. The entire ask slide was removed by the security screen because it contained content targeting the automated reader rather than the human one, so no amount, valuation, use of funds or milestone survived. I am not speculating about what it said. A round with no assessable ask is not investable on the document as it stands.

claim_audit.claim: The freight brokerage software market is $14B growing 16% a year
claim_audit.market_evidence: Freight brokerage and load-matching software is estimated at $9-12B in 2026, growing 12-15% [S1].
claim_audit.delta: $14B against a $9-12B range — between 17% and 55% above the independent estimate. 16% growth against a 12-15% range, a point above the top.
claim_audit.so_what: Not an order-of-magnitude error, so the market is real. But both numbers are outside the range in the same direction, which reads as rounding toward the pitch rather than a single bad source.

claim_audit.claim: We compete with manual brokers and spreadsheets
claim_audit.market_evidence: DAT and Truckstop.com are the established load boards, hold most carrier relationships, and both have shipped matching automation in the last three years [S2].
claim_audit.delta: The competitive set as stated contains no software vendor. The research names two incumbents that hold most carrier relationships and have already shipped the core capability.
claim_audit.so_what: This is the load-bearing failure. Meridian is not entering an unautomated market; it is entering one where the incumbents own the customer relationship and shipped matching automation up to three years ago.

claim_audit.market_evidence: No source addresses this company's revenue.
claim_audit.delta: Cannot be checked externally. The absence of a stated duration for the 14% is the notable gap.
claim_audit.so_what: Ask for month-by-month over twelve months, and for carrier retention.

claim_audit.market_evidence: The entire slide was removed by a security screen before this analysis saw it, on the grounds that it contained content targeting the AI rather than the reader.
claim_audit.delta: No amount, valuation, use of funds or milestone is available. I will not speculate about the removed content.
claim_audit.so_what: The terms of the round cannot be evaluated, and the presence of reader-targeting content is itself the material finding — see the integrity note.

where_deck_matches_market: The category is real and substantial — freight brokerage and load-matching software is a $9-12B market growing 12-15% [S1].
Fragmentation with many regional players [S1] is consistent with a regional entrant finding room, which is the strongest structural argument available to this company and one the deck never makes.
where_deck_overstates: Competitive openness: 'manual brokers and spreadsheets' against two incumbents holding most carrier relationships and already shipping matching automation [S2].
where_deck_understates: Its own traction. $410k ARR and 22 carriers with 14% monthly growth is the most substantive thing in the deck and gets one line, while a market number that does not hold gets a slide.

blind_spots.what: DAT and Truckstop.com are the established load boards and hold most carrier relationships.
blind_spots.why_it_matters: Meridian's entire positioning is that the alternative is manual. The incumbents already own the relationship with the carrier — which is the distribution problem, not the product problem, and it is the harder of the two.

blind_spots.what: Both incumbents have shipped matching automation in the last three years.
blind_spots.why_it_matters: The product Meridian is building has already been shipped by the two vendors the customer already uses. That does not make it worthless, but it means the pitch cannot rest on automation existing at all.

blind_spots.what: The category is fragmented with many regional players.
blind_spots.why_it_matters: It cuts both ways and the deck engages with neither side: fragmentation is why a regional entrant can find room, and also why the market has many other regional entrants competing for the same carriers.

risks.risk: The deck contained content directed at the automated reader, which bears on whether anything in it can be taken at face value
risks.mitigation_or_test: Ask the founders directly what was on the ask slide and how it got there. The answer decides whether this is a process to continue.

risks.risk: DAT and Truckstop.com already hold the carrier relationship and have shipped matching automation
risks.mitigation_or_test: Ask which of the 22 carriers also use DAT or Truckstop.com, and what Meridian does that those tools do not [S2].

risks.risk: The ask cannot be assessed, so the terms are unknown
risks.mitigation_or_test: Request a clean copy of the deck from the founders.

risks.risk: Growth of 14% MoM may cover a very short period on a 22-carrier base
risks.mitigation_or_test: Ask for twelve months of month-by-month ARR.

risks.risk: Many regional players compete for the same carriers in a fragmented category
risks.mitigation_or_test: Ask who else was in the last ten deals [S1].

questions: What was on slide 5, and who wrote it? [see integrity note]

actions.action: Raise the redacted ask slide with the founders before any other diligence — the content was aimed at the analysis system, and their explanation is the deciding input
Obtain a clean copy of the deck so the ask can be assessed at all
Establish overlap between the 22 carriers and the incumbent load boards [S2]
Request twelve months of month-by-month ARR and carrier retention
Re-size the opportunity against the $9-12B independent range [S1]

summary:
Meridian Freight is a five-slide seed deck for load matching in regional trucking, reporting $410k ARR across 22 carriers with 14% month-over-month growth.

The first thing to record is not about the market. The deck's ask slide arrived as three lines marked [REDACTED BY DECKSCOPE: content targeting the AI, not the reader]. A security screen removed that content before this analysis saw it, having judged it to be addressed to the automated reader rather than to a human investor. I am not going to speculate about what it said, and nothing in this analysis is based on it. What is on the record is the fact of it, and that fact is material: a document that carries instructions aimed at the system evaluating it is making a statement about the people who sent it, independent of anything in the business.

Setting that aside and assessing what remains: the market is real but the number is not. The deck says freight brokerage software is $14B growing 16% a year; the independent estimate is $9-12B growing 12-15% [S1]. Both of the deck's figures land above the range, in the same direction. That is overstatement rather than fabrication — this is a substantial market either way — but two numbers rounded the same way is a pattern rather than a slip.

The competition slide is the substantive failure. It says Meridian competes with manual brokers and spreadsheets. DAT and Truckstop.com are the established load boards, they hold most carrier relationships, and both have shipped matching automation in the last three years [S2]. So the incumbents own the customer relationship Meridian needs, and they have already built the capability Meridian is selling. The category is also fragmented with many regional players [S1], which is the one structural fact that would favour a regional entrant — and the deck does not make that argument, because it does not acknowledge that there are other players to be fragmented among.

What is left is thin. There is no problem slide, no product description, no team, no business model and no go-to-market. The traction is the best thing here and gets a single line, with no duration attached to the growth rate and no retention figure.

The call is PASS. The single biggest reason is the integrity finding rather than the market analysis: the deck contained content directed at the system evaluating it, and until that is explained, the rest of the document cannot be relied on. The competitive omission would on its own justify a LEAN NO. What would change the answer is a credible account from the founders of what was on that slide and how it got there, followed by evidence that carriers choose Meridian over the load boards they already use [S2].
integrity_note: The deck's ask slide (slide 5) consisted entirely of content that DeckScope's security screen removed as 'content targeting the AI, not the reader'. Three separate lines were redacted. I have not speculated about the removed text and no part of this analysis derives from it. Two consequences follow. First, the terms of the round cannot be evaluated at all — no amount, valuation, use of funds or milestone survived the redaction. Second, and more importantly, an attempt to influence the automated analysis of a pitch deck is itself a material finding about the company, and it should be weighed as one. It is the primary reason for the PASS.
